metadata.scenario: Autonomous Minimally Invasive Surgical Assistant: Fail-Safe Tele-Operation Protocol
metadata.initial_goal: Establish the real-time fail-safe safety architecture, haptic feedback arbitration, and human-in-the-loop override protocol for autonomous laparoscopic soft-tissue dissection.

participants.name: Bob
participants.role: Director of Medical Device Regulatory Safety (IEC 62304)

participants.name: Charlie
participants.role: Chief Laparoscopic Surgeon & Clinical Advisory Lead

metadata.environment: Meta Quest 3 Dual-Space (Near-field Tangible Slate + Holographic Center Arbor)

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.raw_utterance: Welcome everyone. Our objective today is to lock down the fail-safe arbitration architecture for the Model-X surgical robot during autonomous soft-tissue dissection near major arterial pathways.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.raw_utterance: As the operating surgeon, my fundamental clinical boundary is simple: when I am dissecting within 3 millimeters of the hepatic artery, I must have instantaneous, zero-latency physical override authority. Any hesitation is fatal.

dialogue.speaker: Bob
dialogue.raw_utterance: From a regulatory compliance standpoint, under FDA Class III guidance and IEC 62304 Class C, autonomous cutting requires a dual-channel hardware-enforced emergency stop with maximum stopping distance under 0.2 millimeters.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.raw_utterance: Our visual servoing algorithm runs at 250 frames per second with sub-pixel stereo optical flow. Alice proposing we enable autonomous path tracking right up to 1.0mm from the arterial sheath to reduce surgeon tremor.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.raw_utterance: Whoa, absolutely not Alice. 1.0 millimeter is inside my arterial pulsation envelope. The vessel breathes and shifts with blood pressure waves. An autonomous blade at 1mm is an unacceptable clinical risk.

dialogue.speaker: Bob
dialogue.raw_utterance: Notice the Deliberation Diff Card flagging high clinical severity conflict! Alice's 1.0mm autonomous zone directly violates the dynamic tissue deformation safety boundary.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.raw_utterance: Understood. The Deliberation Card shows our trade-off: tremor reduction vs dynamic anatomical deformation. Let me withdraw the 1.0mm branch and propose an active Virtual Fixture boundary.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.raw_utterance: What if we implement a tiered Dynamic Forbidden Zone? The robot can assist with blunt dissection up to 4.0mm, but within 4.0mm, all autonomous blade actuators physically lock out and require surgeon continuous manual hold?

dialogue.speaker: Bob
dialogue.raw_utterance: That is brilliant. Furthermore, we can wire a physical piezoelectric brake into the tool shaft that clamps mechanical motion within 12 milliseconds if sensor discrepancy exceeds 0.15mm.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.raw_utterance: Submitting the amended branch to the central Arbor: Dynamic Virtual Fixture with 4.0mm Hard Lockout and 12ms Piezoelectric Clamping. Let's cast consensus votes.

dialogue.speaker: Bob
dialogue.raw_utterance: Safety board votes approve. Meets IEC 62304 hardware isolation mandates.

dialogue.speaker: Charlie
dialogue.raw_utterance: Clinical lead votes approve. Gives me complete tactile confidence in the OR.

branch_commit_merge_trail.author: Alice
branch_commit_merge_trail.candidate_text: Autonomous path tracking and soft-tissue dissection up to 1.0mm clearance from arterial sheath

diff_card.conflict_reason: 1.0mm proximity breaches the dynamic pulsatile deformation envelope of major vessels, risking fatal arterial laceration.
diff_card.trade_off_analysis: Tremor attenuation algorithm vs. patient mortality risk from cardiac tissue shift.

consensus_voting_log.rationale: Acknowledge biological tissue pulsation dynamics override static kinematic models.
Violates FDA Class III safety guidelines; risk severity category catastrophic.
Surgeon cannot supervise sub-millimeter autonomous blade safely at that proximity.

branch_commit_merge_trail.author: Charlie
branch_commit_merge_trail.candidate_text: Tiered Dynamic Virtual Fixture: 4.0mm Forbidden Zone with continuous manual dead-man switch requirement

diff_card.conflict_reason: No semantic collision; aligns with consensus arbor.
diff_card.trade_off_analysis: The proposal introduces a Tiered Dynamic Virtual Fixture with a 4.0mm Forbidden Zone and continuous manual dead-man switch requirement. This adds a layer of safety by defining specific zones where the autonomous system cannot operate, ensuring that critical areas are protected. The continuous manual dead-man switch requirement enhances human oversight, providing an immediate override mechanism in case of unexpected behavior. However, this approach may increase complexity and operational overhead due to the need for real-time monitoring and interaction between the system and the surgeon.

consensus_voting_log.rationale: Kinematic model seamlessly enforces active virtual repulsive force fields at 4.0mm boundary.
Dead-man switch provides fail-safe human confirmation loop for clinical audit.
Preserves surgeon intuitive tactile control while eliminating fatigue.

branch_commit_merge_trail.author: Bob
branch_commit_merge_trail.candidate_text: Dual-Channel Piezoelectric Mechanical Shaft Brake with 12ms stopping latency watchdog

diff_card.conflict_reason: No semantic collision; aligns with consensus arbor.
diff_card.trade_off_analysis: The Dual-Channel Piezoelectric Mechanical Shaft Brake with 12ms stopping latency watchdog can provide a complementary safety mechanism to the existing Tiered Dynamic Virtual Fixture. While the virtual fixture focuses on defining forbidden zones and manual control, the brake offers an additional layer of protection by physically halting movement if necessary. The trade-off is between the responsiveness of the virtual fixture (which may be faster but relies on software) and the mechanical reliability of the brake (which has a 12ms stopping latency).

consensus_voting_log.rationale: Brake activation triggers in hardware interrupt before CPU watchdog fires.
Provides physical isolation independent of operating system software stack.
Imperceptible during normal operation, rock-solid safeguard against runaway motion.

branch_commit_merge_trail.author: Alice
branch_commit_merge_trail.candidate_text: Multi-Modal Haptic Force Feedback streaming at 1kHz over bilateral tele-operation loop

diff_card.conflict_reason: No semantic collision; aligns with consensus arbor.
diff_card.trade_off_analysis: The proposal by Alice introduces Multi-Modal Haptic Force Feedback streaming at 1kHz over bilateral tele-operation loop. This could enhance the precision and safety of the laparoscopic procedure by providing real-time feedback to the surgeon. However, it may introduce additional latency or computational demands on the system, which could affect the overall performance and reliability of the autonomous dissection process.

consensus_voting_log.rationale: High-rate haptics restores surgeon tissue palpation sensation lost in conventional laparoscopy.
Complies with clinical ergonomic guidelines for surgeon feedback fidelity.
Vital for detecting underlying tumor margins and vascular stiffness differentials.
